test.title: A song that is special to you

document.cue: Describe a song that is special to you.

text: The song I'd like to talk about is 'Here Comes the Sun' by the Beatles. It was written by George Harrison and came out in 1969, so it's much older than me, but it's probably the song I've listened to more than any other.

I first heard it when I was about ten, in my uncle's car on a long drive from Almaty to Balkhash. He had a CD of Beatles songs, and this was the only one I asked him to play again and again. I didn't understand most of the English then, but I loved the guitar at the beginning and how light and happy it sounded.

It's a simple song about the end of a long, cold winter and the relief of seeing the sun again. Later I read that Harrison wrote it in a friend's garden on a spring day when he'd escaped from stressful business meetings, which makes sense when you listen to it — it sounds like someone finally breathing out.

It's special to me because it has become my personal signal that a hard period is ending. I played it the morning after my final school exam, and again when I got my first job offer. It also reminds me of my uncle, who taught me that old music isn't boring at all.
Whenever the first warm day of spring comes, it's the first song I put on.
